verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              क्लिश्यमानेषु भूतेषु तैस्तैर्भावैस्ततस्ततः। दुर्गाण्यतितरेद्येन तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said O grandfather you are endued with great wisdom and thoroughly grounded in every branch of learning. From this very narrative of the destruction of Vritra the wish has arisen in my mind of asking you a question.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              आश्रमेषु यथोक्तेषु यथोक्तं ये द्विजातयः। वर्तन्ते संयतात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२॥
verses.english: You have said, O king, that Vritra was Stupefied by Fever, and that then, O sinless one, he was killed by Vasava with the thunderboli.

verses.sanskrit: ये दम्भान्नाचरन्ति स्म येषां वृत्तिश्च संयता। विषयांश्च निगृह्णन्ति दुर्गाण्यतरन्ति ते॥३॥
verses.english: How did this Fever, O you of great wisdom, originale, O lord, I wish to hear fully of the origin of Fever,

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्याहुर्नोच्यमाना ये न हिंसन्ति च हिंसिताः। प्रयच्छन्ति न याचन्ते दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥४॥
verses.english: Listen, O king, to the origin, known all over the world, of Fever! I shall describe fully this topic, fully explaining how Fever first came into existence, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: वासयन्त्यतिथीन्नित्यं नित्यं ये चानसूयकाः। नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलाश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥५॥
verses.english: In days of yore, O king, there was a summit, named Savitri, of the mountains of Meru. Adored of all the worlds, it was endued with great effulgence and adorned with every sort of jewels and gems.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रापित्रोश्च ये वृत्तिं वर्तन्ते धर्मकोविदाः। वर्जयन्ति दिवा स्वप्नं दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥६॥
verses.english: That summit was immeasurable in extent and no one could go there. On that mountain summit the divine Mahadeva used to sit shiningly as if on a bed-stead adorned with gold.

verses.sanskrit: ये वा पापं न कुर्वन्ति कर्मणा, मनसा, गिरा। निक्षिप्तदण्डा भूतेषु दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥७॥
verses.english: Sitting by his side, the daughter of the king of mountains shone in brilliance. The great gods, the Vasus of immeasurable energy, the great Ashvins, those foremost of physicians, and king Vaishravana attended by many a Guhyaka,-that king of the Yakshas, endued with prosperity and power, and having his abode on the suminit of Kailasa,-all waited upon the great Mahadeva. And the great sage Ushanas, and the foremost of Rishis headed by Sanatkumara, and the other celestial Rishis headed by Angiras, and the Gandharva Vishvavasu, and Narada and Parvata, and the various clans of Apsaras, all came there to wait upon the king of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: ये न लोभान्नयन्त्यर्थान् राजानो रजसाऽन्विताः। विषयान् परिरक्षन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥८॥
verses.english: A pure and auspicious air carrying various sorts of perfumes, blew there. The trees that stood there were adorned with the flowers of all seasons.

verses.sanskrit: स्वेषु दारेषु वर्तन्ते न्यायवृत्तिमृतावृतौ। अग्निहोत्रपराः सन्तो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥९॥
verses.english: A large number of Vidyadharas, Siddhas and ascetics, too, O Bharata, went there for waiting upon Mahadeva, that Lord of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: आहवेषु च ये शूरास्त्यक्त्वा मरणजं भयम्। धर्मेण जयमिच्छन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१०॥
verses.english: Many ghosts also, of various forms and aspects, and many fearful Rakshasas and powerful Pishachas, of various forms, mad with joy, and armed with various sorts of uplifted weapons forming the train of Mahadeva, were there, every one of whom looked like a blazing fire energy.

verses.sanskrit: ये वदन्तीह सत्यानि प्राणत्यागेऽप्युपस्थिते। प्रमाणभूता भूतानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥११॥
verses.english: The illustrious Nandi stood there obeying the great god, shining with his own energy and armed with a lance that resembled a flame of fire.

verses.sanskrit: कर्माण्यकुहकार्थानि येषां वाचश्च सूनृताः। येषामाश्च सम्बद्धा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१२॥
verses.english: Ganga, also, that foremost of all Rivers and originating from all sacred waters in the universe, waited there in her embodied form, O son of Kuru, upon that illustrious gods.

verses.sanskrit: अनध्यायेषु ये विप्राः स्वाध्यायं नेह कुर्वते। तपोनिष्ठाः सुतपसो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१३॥
verses.english: Thus worshipped by the celestial Rishis and the gods, the illustrious Mahadeva of great energy lived on that summit of Meru.

verses.sanskrit: ये तपश्च तपस्यन्ति कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः। विद्यावेदव्रतस्नाता दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१४॥
verses.english: After sometime had gone away, the Prajapati Daksha began to celebrate a sacrifice according to ancient rites.

verses.sanskrit: ये च संशान्तरजसः संशान्ततमसश्च ये। सत्त्वे स्थिता महात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१५॥
verses.english: All the gods in a body headed by Sakra, resolved to repair to that sacrifice of Daksha.

verses.sanskrit: येषां न कश्चित्त्रसति न त्रसन्ति हि कस्यचित्। येषामात्मसमो लोको दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१६॥
verses.english: We have heard that the great gods ordered by Mahadeva, mounted their celestial cars resembling the fire or the Sun in sheen, and proceeded to that spot whence the Ganges is said to issue.

verses.sanskrit: परश्रिया न तप्यन्ति ये सन्तः पुरुषर्षभाः। ग्राम्यादर्थानिवृत्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१७॥
verses.english: Seeing the deities depart, the excellent daughter of the king of mountains, addressed her divine husband, viz., the Lord of all creatures, and said, O illustrious one, who are those gods headed by Shakra going? O you who know the truth, tell me truly, for a great doubt has possessed my mind.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वान्देवान्नमस्यन्ति सर्वधर्मांश्च शृण्वते। ये श्रद्दधानाः शान्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१८॥
verses.english: Maheshvara said 0 highly blessed lady, the excellent Prajapati Daksha is worshipping the gods in a House Sacrifice! These Dwellers of heaven are going there.

verses.sanskrit: ये न मानित्वमिच्छन्ति मानयन्ति च ये परान्। मान्यमानान्नमस्यन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥१९॥
verses.english: Uma said Why, O Mahadeva do you not go to that Sacrifice? What objection is there of your going to that place?

verses.sanskrit: ये च श्राद्धानि कुर्वन्ति तिथ्यां तिथ्यां प्रजार्थिनः। सुविशुद्धेन मनसा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२०॥
verses.english: O highly blessed lady, the gods in days of yore made a compact by virtue of which no share was allotted to me of offerings in all Sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: ये क्रोधं संनियच्छन्ति क्रुद्धान्संशमयन्ति च। न च कुप्यन्ति भूतानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२१॥
verses.english: According to that arrangement, O fair one, the gods do not give me, following the old custom, any share of the sacrificial offerings!

verses.sanskrit: मधु मांसं च ये नित्यं वर्जयन्तीह मानवाः। जन्मप्रभृति मद्यं च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२२॥
verses.english: Uma said-O illustrious one, among all gods, you are the foremost in prowess. In merit, in energy, in fame, and in prosperity you are second to none, and you are, indeed superior to all.

verses.sanskrit: यात्रार्थं भोजनं येषां संतानार्थं च मैथुनम्। वाक् सत्यवचनार्थाय दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२३॥
verses.english: On account, however, of this disability regarding a share I am filled with great grief, O sinless one, and a treinour fills me from head to foot.

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वरं सर्वभूतानां जगतः प्रभवाप्ययम्। भक्ता नारायणं देवं दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२४॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Having said these words to her consort, the Lord of all creatures, O monarch, the goddess Parvati remained silent, her heart burning the while in grief.

verses.sanskrit: य एष पद्मरक्ताक्षः पीतवासा महाभुजः। सुहृद्भ्राता च मित्रं च सम्बन्धी च तथाऽच्युतः॥२५॥
verses.english: Then, understanding what was in her heart and what her thoughts were (for wiping off that disgrace), Mahadeva addressed Nandi, saying,-Wait here.

verses.sanskrit: य इमान्सकलाँल्लोकांश्चर्मवत्परिवेष्टयेत्। इच्छन्प्रभुरचिन्त्यात्मा गोविन्दः पुरुषोत्तमः॥२६॥
verses.english: Summoning all his Yoga powers, that Lord of all lords of Yoga, that god of gods, that holder of Pinaka, possessed of great energy, quickly proceeded to the place accompanied by all his dreadful followers and destroyed that Sacrifice. Of these followers of his, some yelled, and some laughed terribly, and some, O king, extinguished the fires with blood; and some, having dreadful faces, pulling up the sacrificial stakes, began to whirl them. Others began to devour those that were celebrating the Sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: स्थितः प्रियहिते जिष्णोः स एष पुरुषोत्तमः। राजंस्तव च दुर्धर्षो वैकुण्ठः पुरुषर्षभ॥२७॥
verses.english: Then thus afflicted on every side, that Sacrifice, assumed the form of a deer and tried to fly away through the firmanent.

verses.sanskrit: य एनं संश्रयन्तीह भक्ता नारायणं हरिम्। ते तरन्तीह दुर्गाणि न चात्रास्ति विचारणा॥२८॥
verses.english: Learning that the Sacrifice was running away in that form, the powerful Mahadeva began to pursue him with bow and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्गातितरणं ये च पठन्ति श्रावयन्ति च। कथयन्ति च विप्रेभ्यो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥२९॥
verses.english: On account of the ire which then filled the heart of that foremost of all gods, possessed of matchless energy, a dreadful drop of sweat appeared on his forehead.

verses.sanskrit: इति कृत्यसमुद्देशः कीर्तितस्ते मयाऽनघ। तरन्ते येन दुर्गाणि परत्रेह च मानवाः॥३०॥
verses.english: When the drop of sweat fell down on the Earth, there immediately appeared a blazing fire resembling the conflagration that appears at the end of the cycle.
